newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds build on tentative support.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds build on tentative support.

text.p: *Australian bonds pared an initial steep fall by the close after finding a supportive, albeit tentative, base with many hurdles to cross in the next few days.
*Latest on enterprise bargaining agreements due Wednesday.
Australian bonds pared an initial steep price fall by the close after finding a supportive, albeit tentative, base with several hurdles locally and in the U.S. to overcome in the next few days.

The benchmark November 2006 bond yield spiked 10 basis points to around 7.60 percent just after the opening amid a combination offshore selling, weak technicals and fairly bruised market sentiment, traders said.
"Tentative is the best way to describe current support, and I don't think things are going to change this side of the Humphrey-Hawkins," said one trader at a European based bank.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivers the first instalment of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday, although the second-leg has been postponed until March 5 instead of Thursday.

Locally, wages data over the next two days is expected to occupy the market with the latest report on enterprise bargaining agreements from the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR) expected on Wednesday.
Rob Henderson, chief economist at Dresdner, said the key interest in the DIR release would be in whether private sector wages growth had slowed further.
"An outcome in the high four percent area, as we expect, would be a plus for the inflation outlook," he said.
Private sector wages rose 5.3 percent in the December quarter, down from 6.1 percent in the previous quarter.
Thursday sees final average weekly earnings data for the November quarter, as will another part of the fourth quarter GDP picture in the shape of capital expenditure.
The full GDP release is due on March 5.

Although the local market reclaimed most of its initial spread widening against the U.S., it underperformed Canada after S&P upgraded Canada's foreign currency debt rating outlook to stable from negative on Monday. A switch to Canadian debt from Australia was cited as one factor in the initial sell-off.

The 10-year bond contract bounced off support at 92.370, but not until after last week's 92.450 low and the 61.8 percent retracement of the early-January/mid-Feb rally at 92.415 had been breached. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
